title: Am I too weird to date?
old_caption:
Worried you're too much of yourself to date? The right person likes your weird, rocks with faces and all.
Lead with who you really are. It helps the right ones find you.

title: Should I make the first move?
old_caption:
Thinking about making the first move? A simple "want to get coffee?" absolutely counts.
Then give them room to answer, with no pressure. Go first, then go easy.

title: They want me to meet their family.
old_caption:
Meeting their family can make anyone nervous. Bring something small, ask them one question about themselves, and lean on your date if you need to.
Family isn't a test. Show up warm, and that's enough.

title: I'm too busy to date.
old_caption:
Feeling too busy for love is real, and so is the truth that busy people deserve it too.
One evening a week, phone in a drawer. If you make room, you can show up fully.

title: I never know what to say.
old_caption:
Blanking on what to say is so common. Try asking what made them laugh this week, then really listen.
Follow-up questions do the rest. Being curious about someone is quietly charming.

title: How do I give a real compliment?
old_caption: Want to give a compliment that really lands? Skip "you look nice" and name something specific you noticed. Small details show someone you were paying attention.

title: We can never pick where to eat.
old_caption: Can't ever agree on where to eat? Take turns: you choose Tuesday, they choose Friday. Fairness is easier when it's a simple plan instead of a feeling you keep weighing.

title: How do I get over someone?
old_caption:
Getting over someone hurts, and it's okay to cry about it. Then unfollow, call a friend, get some fresh air and some water.
One day you'll notice they didn't cross your mind. Feel it, then let it go.

title: Is it okay to want space?
old_caption: Is wanting space okay? Yes. "I need a night to myself" isn't a breakup, it's honesty. Say it kindly, say when you'll be back, and let space be part of a healthy love.

title: How do I know if I can trust them?
old_caption: How do you know if you can trust someone? Watch whether their words and actions match over weeks, not one big moment. And ask. Trust gets built slowly, brick by brick.
